name: Dume
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: The tone system of Ts'amakko is based on a high tone and a low tone and has limited function load. It is not the case to make a full explanation of it in the present paper, as it suffices to state that, with some exception, tone is not marked in the Grammar of Ts'amakko. This is because the grammar provides information about the tonal characteristics of almost all word classes and verb paradigms and tone placement can be predicted from this information. An exception are those nominals that do not follow the default patterns HL or HHL. In these cases, tone is marked.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The language the name 'Dume' denotes (Ts'amakko/Tsamai) is described as a two-tone (H/L) language with low functional load; tone placement is predictable by word class and verb paradigm, and nominals default to HL or HHL melodies. No statement about word stress is made; the author uses 'accent' only for Ongota (sec. 3.1.3).
new_statements.exceptions: Nominals not following the default HL / HHL patterns (tone lexically marked for these).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone melodies in citation forms as transcribed for the grammar; nothing on phrase-level prosody.
new_statements.identity_note: dume1236 is not a language: it is a retired Glottolog bookkeeping languoid (hid NOCODE_Dume) generated from two ethnographic notices (Schlichter 1897 'Notiz..'; Pauli 1950 'Rudolfsees'; md.ini triggers 'notiz', 'rudolfsees'). Glottolog's own bibliography annotates the name in Bryan 1945 and Pauli 1950 as 'Dume = Tsamai [tsb]', and Wikipedia's Tsamai page carries dume1236 as a second Glottolog code, calling Dume ('pseudo-pygmies') an apparent variety of Tsamai. The language the name denotes is therefore Tsamai / Ts'amakko, tsam1247 (ISO tsb; East Cushitic, Dullay), which already has a held statement (Savà 2021, tonal). Do not confuse with the Chadic dialect Dume (Vame), dume1239, Cameroon. by our rule that each source is filed under the language's current Glottolog code (a retired code does not make a separate language) a retired code does not make a separate language: the catalog entry belongs to tsam1247, and dume1236 should be dropped from the target list as a duplicate.

new_statements.quote: Here are examples of sentences with =ma. Notice that the first syllable of the word =ma attaches to is lengthened and the accent moves to the last syllable. Examples of =ma marking destination: (20) daal-issa kaaysa=ma sor goat-DIST.M/P there=DEST run.IMP.SG 'Run towards those goats!' (21) ʔufo maann-e=ma zow-i SBJ.3SG.M house-P=DEST go-UNM.3SG.M 'He went home.' [fn.4, p.168:] In order to avoid a double clitic, the possessor is indicated by lengthening on the first syllable vowel.

new_statements.relation_note: No catalog record exists for dume1236. The existing statement of record (Savà 2021, sec. 2.1.3) describes Ts'amakko as having a high/low 'tone system' of limited functional load and gives no stress placement. This 2020 chapter by the same author is compatible and adds one morphophonological detail: a culminative 'accent' that shifts to the host-final syllable under =ma cliticisation. It neither states a default accent position nor contradicts the 2021 tone statement; the difference is terminological (accent 2020 vs tone 2021).
new_statements.rule_in_words: No general word-stress/accent placement rule is given. The chapter is morphosyntactic (case clitics =ta, =ma, =nu/=un) and has no phonology or prosody section. The only prosodic statement is incidental: when the destination clitic =ma attaches to a word, that host's first syllable is lengthened and 'the accent' moves to the host's last syllable (i.e. the syllable immediately before =ma). This presupposes a single movable word accent but does not say where it falls by default or whether it is realised as pitch or stress.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the accent shift is stated only for hosts of =ma (accompanied by first-syllable vowel lengthening); fn.4 adds that a possessor before =ta can be marked by first-syllable vowel lengthening alone.
new_statements.identity_note: dume1236 'Dume' is a retired Glottolog bookkeeping languoid whose name Glottolog's bibliography equates with Tsamai / Ts'amakko (tsam1247, East Cushitic, Dullay cluster). The work read describes Ts'amakko as documented in Savà's 2005 Leiden grammar (speakers of the Weyt'o valley, Bena-Tsamai Woreda, South Omo Zone); it says nothing about a variety called Dume. Any statement here belongs under tsam1247.

sources.note: Bibliographic records only. Bryan 1945 and Pauli 1950 carry the language code annotation 'Dume = Tsamai [tsb]' (Pauli also 'Kule = Ts'amakko [tsb]'); Schlichter 1897 langnote 'Dume, Bunno, Doko, Aro, Mala (locations mentioned)'. All three are overview/ethnographic notices, none a phonology.
Nothing on prosody. Infobox lists both Glottolog codes 'tsam1247 Tsamai' and 'dume1236 Dume'; text: 'Cule (Kuile, Kule) and evidently Dume (pseudo-pygmies) were apparently varieties' of Tsamai.
